title: Read-only share links for project boards
brief: Owners can now create a public, read-only link to a board, pick when it expires, and revoke it. Links are stored as SHA-256 hashes, and a project flips to *Shared by link* while any link is live.

risk.why: Adds the first unauthenticated route (`GET /s/:token`). The *Never* expiry option can't actually be chosen, and expired links keep a board marked as shared.

summary: New `share_links` table (hashed tokens, expiry, soft revoke) and a `projects.visibility` column.
Three routes: create and revoke links (owners only), plus a public `GET /s/:token` that returns the board read-only.
New `canShare` permission: owners only. Editors keep rename but can't share.
Project header gets a **Share** button and a *Shared by link* pill; the button opens a new share popover.
Tests for token hashing, expiry, revocation, and the new permission.

focus.title: The public route
focus.why: First endpoint with no session. Check it can only ever return a board's id and name.

focus.title: Expiry default swallows “Never”
focus.why: `null ?? 7` is `7`, so the popover's *Never* option silently becomes 7 days.

focus.title: Token storage and lookup
focus.why: Raw token is returned once; only the hash is stored. Expiry and revocation are checked on every resolve.

focus.title: When a board stops being “shared”
focus.why: Visibility is recomputed on revoke but not on expiry.

blocks.title: Migration is additive
blocks.md: `002_share_links.sql` only creates a table and adds a defaulted column, so it's safe to run on a live database. There is no down migration.

blocks.summary: Unchanged, but the new `ON DELETE CASCADE` depends on it.

annotations.text: SQLite ignores foreign keys unless this pragma is on, so deleting a project only removes its links because of this line.

endpoints.summary: Create a link. Returns the raw token exactly once, inside `url`.

params.name: ttlDays
params.note: Defaults to 7. `null` is meant to mean *never*, but is currently coerced to 7.

endpoints.summary: Soft-revoke a link. If no live links remain, the project goes back to `private`.
Resolve a token to a read-only board. Unknown, expired, and revoked tokens all return the same 404.

blocks.caption: How a visitor's request is resolved. The token is hashed before the lookup, so the database never sees it.
blocks.source:
sequenceDiagram
  participant V as Link visitor
  participant R as GET /s/:token
  participant S as resolveShareLink
  participant DB as share_links
  V->>R: /s/k3J9…x2Qa
  R->>S: token
  S->>S: sha256(token)
  S->>DB: WHERE token_hash = ?
  DB-->>S: row or nothing
  alt revoked, expired, or missing
    S-->>R: null
    R-->>V: 404 link_not_found
  else live
    S-->>R: { projectId }
    R-->>V: 200 { id, name } read-only
  end

keyChanges.summary: Adds the create, revoke, and public resolve routes. Create and revoke are gated on the new `canShare`; the public route needs no session.

annotations.text: Gate is `canShare`, not `canEdit` — editors get a 403 here.
`req.body.ttlDays ?? 7` turns an explicit `null` (the popover's *Never*) into 7. Use `'ttlDays' in req.body ? req.body.ttlDays : 7`.
The only place the raw token ever leaves the server.
Public route. It selects only `id, name`, so board contents aren't exposed by this route alone. Unknown, expired, and revoked tokens all return the same 404, so a visitor can't tell them apart.

keyChanges.summary: New module that owns token generation, hashing, lookup, and revocation, and keeps `projects.visibility` in sync.

annotations.text: Tokens are hashed with SHA-256 before storage, so a database leak doesn't leak working links.
The insert and the visibility update aren't in a transaction. Fine for SQLite in practice, but worth a `db.transaction` if this moves to Postgres.
Expiry is enforced at read time — nothing deletes old rows.
Counts links with `revoked_at IS NULL` but ignores `expires_at`. When every link has simply expired, the project stays `link` and keeps showing *Shared by link*.

keyChanges.summary: Header renders the *Shared by link* pill and an owner-only **Share** button that toggles the popover.

annotations.text: Re-implements `canShare` on the client instead of importing it. Harmless today; the server check is the real gate.
Pill is driven by `project.visibility`, so it inherits the expiry issue in `shareLinks.ts`.

keyChanges.summary: Creates `share_links` and adds `projects.visibility` with a default, so existing rows need no backfill.

annotations.text: Links are deleted with their project.
SQLite allows `ADD COLUMN` with a `CHECK` because the default satisfies it.

questions: Should *Never expires* exist at all for public links, or should 90 days be the ceiling?
Should editors be allowed to create links, or is owners-only right?

verified.text: New unit tests cover token hashing, expiry, revocation, and `canShare`.

verified: Migration applies cleanly on a copy of the seed database.
